title: Add a cross-target check matrix now that the workspace is pure Rust
description:
39d0331 removed ring, and cross-compilation now works from the Linux runner with no extra toolchain. Measured there:
  persona-core -> aarch64-apple-darwin      exit 0
  persona-core -> x86_64-pc-windows-msvc    exit 0
  persona-core -> aarch64-unknown-linux-ohos exit 0
  whole workspace -> aarch64-apple-darwin    exit 0

cargo check runs build scripts but never links, so a plain ubuntu runner needs no cross linker and no extra install step.

This supersedes persona-vvs2.1, which proposed a windows-latest job limited to persona-core. A cross-check matrix is strictly better: it covers every target from one runner, costs no extra runner minutes, and catches Unix-only code entering a crate that is supposed to stay portable — which is the actual failure mode, since persona-core holds the crypto and the pseudonym derivation.

Suggested: a job running cargo check --target <t> -p persona-core for the three targets, plus --workspace for aarch64-apple-darwin. Do NOT add --workspace for Windows: persona-grpc is still Unix-only by design, 21 UnixListener/UnixStream sites, tracked by this epic's parent. Widen per crate as the transport abstraction lands.
